text: Stationary obstacles. Well, then the fading multipath fading is still there as a phenomenon, but it's not that serious. Why? Because if you have chairs, walls, wardrobes, the geometry of the scenario is stationary or slowly changing, like in this case in this classroom now. Well, then, as actually the communication don't, you have the possibility to estimate the channel, to understand what kind of scenario you have got, what kind of shape of fading you have got. Because things do not change, so everything is more or less fixed. So you can estimate the power that the receiver gets and compensate for that. So if the receiver gets a weak signal because of fading or multipath fading, you can say, well, I will increase my transmission power. So you can compensate for the attenuation that the signal experiences. That's the lucky case where you have this so called slow fading, slow changing fade. That is also called shadowing. The nasty phenomenon is the so called fast fading. When your scenario is not stationary or slowly changing, your scenario changes very frequently.
